ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the circuit, point A is a node on the left side; from A to the right, it connects through a 12Ω resistor to the right-side vertical wire node, and a ground symbol is drawn below this right-side node, so the potential of this node is 0V. Point A connects downward through a 36Ω resistor to the terminal labeled -24V. The right-side ground node also connects upward through a 24Ω resistor to the +12V terminal, but this branch is not directly connected to A. Reasoning: Taking the right-side ground node as the reference ground, let the potential of point A be VA. Point A has no current source injection, and by KCL the sum of currents flowing out of A is 0: VA/12 + (VA + 24)/36 = 0. Multiplying both sides by 36: 3VA + VA + 24 = 0, therefore 4VA = -24, VA = -6V.
